title: Trailing command args lose argv boundaries in launch resolution
description:
resolve_inner_command (launch.rs:194) and build_tmux_command (launch.rs:168-172) collapse the already-split trailing argv with trailing.join(" "). Args that contain spaces, quotes, globs, or $ are silently corrupted because the joined string is re-split by the downstream shell.

Example: 'title-preserver --dir ~/p -- vim "my file.txt"' resolves the inner command to 'exec vim my file.txt' — now two arguments instead of one. Same loss for the tmux path: 'tmux new -As dev vim my file.txt'.

This is the clear-cut half of the original #2/#3 review pair: trailing args arrive as structured argv and must stay structured. Fix: shell-quote each trailing arg (e.g. shell_words::quote / a small quoting helper) before joining, for both the bare-shell exec path and the tmux trailing path. Add tests with multi-word and metacharacter args.
acceptance_criteria: Trailing args containing spaces/quotes/globs survive resolution as single arguments; covered by unit tests; both the exec path and tmux-trailing path quote correctly.

title: Observe upstream terminal replies and serialize child-directed injection
description: Add a bounded observation point on terminal/stdin -> child PTY traffic, which currently passes unexamined. Emit typed reply/report observations without consuming bytes merely because they look like an OSC. Give synthetic child-directed replies one serialized write owner shared with ordinary user input. A query owner may explicitly claim a matched reply; untouched user and terminal bytes pass through exactly. Consumers include OSC7501 replies and OSC99 activation/closure/alive/capability reports. Preserve thread/resource lifetime and avoid requiring an async runtime.
acceptance_criteria:
Fragmented upstream sequences produce ordered observations while unchanged bytes reach the child absent an explicit claim.
Concurrent user bytes and injected replies do not interleave within a reply.
Queries/reports are direction-tagged and cannot be confused with child-issued commands.
Shutdown/EOF and failed injection release resources and surface meaningful outcomes.
PTY fixtures cover untouched ordinary input, recognized reports and synthetic replies.
notes: Source: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Order external terminal commands with relayed child output
description: Create one output coordination point for relayed child bytes and external terminal commands such as scripted color writes/queries. Define safe insertion boundaries across read-buffer splits: serializing arbitrary write calls is insufficient if an OSC/DCS/CSI is already partly emitted. Keep buffering bounded with explicit malformed-stream behavior. Record injected dispatch through the state reducer once without looping emitted bytes through observation. Coordinate OSC7501 query interception/reply completion before a following DA probe is sent outward. Byte dispatch is evidence of a request, not proof of terminal application.
acceptance_criteria:
External commands do not splice into split child control sequences; ordinary output order remains intact.
Malformed or unterminated streams follow a bounded documented insertion/forwarding policy.
A query followed by DA in one or split reads obeys the selected responder ordering.
Dispatched writes update recorded/requested state exactly once, with origin metadata, and failed dispatch is not recorded as successful application.
Fake-terminal/PTY fixtures exercise concurrent external writes and streaming child output.
notes: Source: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Route terminal-query replies by origin without leaking them into the shell
description: Coordinate query ownership across supported child-origin and proxy/external-script requests. Legacy/OSC21 color replies lack request IDs, so single-flight among proxy requests alone cannot disambiguate racing child queries. Define a bounded admission/serialization policy over supported visible sources and honest handling of unsupported, ambiguous, late and timed-out replies. Child-origin replies go to the child; matched proxy-origin replies return to the script and must not become unsolicited shell input. Preserve child traffic when ownership is uncertain rather than inventing a successful correlated response. Protocol-specific capability responders remain separate; cached colors are not fresh terminal replies.
acceptance_criteria:
Same-slot child/proxy interleavings, different slots, multiple response chunks and query timeouts are covered with a scripted outer terminal.
A matched proxy reply is consumed by its owner, while child responses and ordinary input remain correctly forwarded.
Late/ambiguous replies follow documented behavior and cannot satisfy the wrong queued request silently.
Outstanding requests, queues and timeouts are bounded; child exit completes pending operations honestly.
The exposed result distinguishes a correlated response from unsupported/unknown/ambiguous outcomes.
notes:
Source: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F
Queried results must retain upstream scope and observation time: an intermediary such as tmux may be the responder, so a captured answer does not universally prove the final physical terminal's configuration. Source: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Coordinate observed and injected terminal traffic across capabilities
description:
Provide the common bidirectional terminal-I/O ownership surface required by status capability replies, notification feedback and externally scriptable colors. Current RelayThreads has an unexamined stdin-to-PTY path and a separate output observer; the new consumers need input observation, ordered injection in both directions, and origin-aware terminal-query routing.

Keep protocol state and presentation decisions in their own capabilities. OSC99 should not depend on the entire OSC7501 implementation merely to observe replies; color queries should not depend on complete notification support. Preserve the lightweight blocking core unless measured evidence supports a change. Children: input observation/child-directed replies; output command coordination; query ownership. Related tipre-tracking-status-responder, tipre-notifications, tipre-colors and tipre-tracking-lightness.
acceptance_criteria:
Shared input/output ownership supports the three consumers without protocol-specific dependencies between them.
Ordinary bytes remain intact and injected units cannot interleave with active protocol frames.
Responses have explicit owners, including child-origin versus external-script queries, ambiguity and timeout.
Scripted-terminal/real-PTY fixtures cover bidirectional ordering and cleanup.
Measured many-instance footprint stays visible through tipre-tracking-lightness.
notes: Factored during review of G notification/color drafts. Source: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Observe kitty OSC 21 color-control sequences into the state model
description:
Current surface: OSC 21 relays unrecorded; existing slots cover only fg/bg/cursor + indexed palette/special.

Scope: route OSC param 21 in src/osc.rs to a ColorControl capture per the PRIMARY kitty spec (sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/color-stack/): SEMICOLON-separated key=value pairs (NOT colons — vtdn is wrong; confirmed kitty window.py color_control value.split(';')). Keys are 0-255 or named (foreground, background, cursor, cursor_text, selection_foreground/background, visual_bell, transparent_background_color1..7 per docs vs 1..8 per kitty source). Value forms: color spec (Set), '?' (Query — capture as query, never a write), empty after '=' (Dynamic), bare key with no '=' (Reset). Numeric keys map onto palette entries; fg/bg/cursor onto existing slots; new named slots for the rest; unknown keys kept verbatim in the capture for logging. Extend re-emit reconstruction for OSC 21 including dynamic and bare-key reset forms. Passthrough only in this ticket — do not answer 21 queries.
design: PROPOSED design pointer, not acceptance: /design/colors/colors0.glm53m.md (OSC 21 authoritative brief). Provenance: opencode://ses_ec7f4e3bcffeQTeR4NqyDYJxS7.
acceptance_criteria: Parser unit tests: all four value forms; batched pairs; numeric-key-to-palette mapping; BEL and ST terminators; unknown keys preserved. Re-emit reconstruction tests covering set, dynamic, and reset forms. Query-bearing sequences recorded as queries, never applied to slots.

title: Accurate color slot state model with a labeled read surface
description:
Current surface: ObservedSlots (src/session.rs) stores Option<ColorSpec> per slot — reset and never-observed are indistinguishable; the parser drops OSC 10-19 chained parameters after the first segment (first_segment in src/osc.rs) although xterm semantics chain each successive Pt to the next dynamic color (so 'OSC 10;red;blue' sets foreground AND background); legacy queries ('4;c;?', '10;?') would be recorded as state writes with spec '?'; ColorSpec normalizes rgb:/rgbi:/# only (named colors and alpha keep raw text, rgb None).

Scope: four-way per-slot state (Set(raw,rgb) / Dynamic / ResetToDefault / never-observed) for fg/bg/cursor, palette, and special entries, raw specs retained; disambiguate legacy queries from writes; fix the chained-parameter divergence; expose a level-labeled read surface (printed snapshot + control-channel 'get') that qualifies recorded state as supported-observed/requested, possibly stale. Re-emit behavior preserved (only retained set values) unless deliberately extended.
design: PROPOSED design pointer, not acceptance: /design/colors/colors0.glm53m.md (state model, legacy verification). Provenance: opencode://ses_ec7f4e3bcffeQTeR4NqyDYJxS7.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: four-way transitions incl. reset-vs-never-observed distinction; 'OSC 10;a;b' records fg AND bg; 'OSC 10;?' captured as query, not a write; named-color specs retain raw with rgb None without error. Read surface returns level-labeled state. Existing relay re-emit tests pass unchanged.

title: Honest, externally readable and eventually writable terminal color state
description:
Current surface: OSC 4/5/10/11/12/104/105/110/111/112 are captured into ObservedSlots (src/session.rs) with latest-value Option semantics, raw+normalized ColorSpec, and exit re-emit under --reemit-title that emits only retained SET values (resets clear slots and are not re-emitted). Gaps: Option conflates reset with never-observed; no dynamic notion; no external read, write, or query; kitty OSC 21 unrecorded; and recorded state is supported-observed/requested — NOT exact current or applied terminal state (terminal defaults, pre-attach writes, multiplexer policy, and unmodeled operations such as color stacks and RIS can all invalidate it).

Scope: an honest four-way slot state model (Set/Dynamic/ResetToDefault/never-observed); a level-labeled read surface distinguishing recorded (possibly stale/unknown-qualified) from queried; kitty OSC 21 observation; an external write path recording dispatched/requested; and an arbitrated query roundtrip with explicit reply-ownership policy. Phasing per child tickets. Out of scope (future scopes needing their own honest stale/unknown view): color stacks (OSC 30001/30101, XTPUSHCOLORS), OSC 6/106 toggles, RIS tracking, tmux-internal color policy. Extends the delivered closed tipre-keep-color-osc capture without re-scoping it; publication stays with the parent-owned tracking/Kopacetic boundary.
design: PROPOSED design pointer, not acceptance: /design/colors/colors0.glm53m.md. Provenance: opencode://ses_ec7f4e3bcffeQTeR4NqyDYJxS7.
acceptance_criteria: Epic-level: every surfaced read distinguishes recorded vs queried levels with the possibly-stale qualification; unmodeled invalidating operations degrade confidence labels toward unknown rather than asserting exact state; external write records dispatched/requested (not proved applied); query results carry an explicit ownership/ambiguity policy. Children define component-level acceptance.

title: Parse and log bare OSC 9 notifications with ConEmu subcommand disambiguation
description:
Current surface: bare OSC 9 relays unrecorded; OSC 9;4 progress was briefed in design/tracking/osc-protocols.glm53m.md and belongs to tipre-tracking-progress.

Scope: record bare 'OSC 9;text' as a notification event (free text payload; no id, no reply, no query) while NOT misreading ConEmu subcommands: data whose first segment matches 'digit;' is subcommand territory (9;4 progress -> tracking epic; 9;9 CWD and 9;12 mark pass through unrecorded for now). Terminals disagree on this split (foot ignores 9;n entirely, Ghostty sniffs the sub-Id, kitty treats bare 9 as the iTerm2 legacy notification) — the observer keys on the first data segment only. Timestamped event into the epic's bounded recent-event window; no re-emit.
design: PROPOSED design pointer, not acceptance: /design/notifications/notifications0.glm53m.md (OSC 9 brief, collision discipline). Provenance: opencode://ses_ec7f4e3bcffeQTeR4NqyDYJxS7.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests in osc.rs: bare notification text captured with BEL and ST terminators; '9;4;...' and other leading-numeric-subcommand forms produce no notification event; recorded event lands in the bounded window. Relay test: byte stream unchanged.
notes: User specifically identified bare OSC9 as work we should be doing alongside current OSC9;4 tracking. Priority aligned to that current protocol surface. Keep notification-vs-ConEmu-subcommand disambiguation explicit. Source: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Observe kitty OSC 99 notifications incl. chunk assembly, ids, and reverse channel strategy
description:
Current surface: OSC 99 bytes relay unrecorded; the current parser data cap (TITLE_CAP=4096, data after ESC ]) cannot hold a maximal legal chunk (up to 4096 encoded payload bytes PLUS the 99 code, metadata section, and separator), so a full-size chunk would be discarded whole as overflow today.

Scope: parse per the PRIMARY kitty spec (sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/desktop-notifications/) — two mandatory semicolons even with empty metadata; colon-separated single-char metadata keys; payload after the second semicolon. Assemble chunked title/body parts per notification id until d!=0 (d is a done flag, NOT a 0/1/2 delivery mode; e is base64, NOT events; o defaults always — vtdn's page is wrong on all three). Decode base64 payloads when e=1; sanitize ids to the identifier grammar before any echo; maintain the derived coalesced outstanding-id view (create/update on same-id events, remove on p=close). Cap accounting per design: size caps against the whole body including framing, plus assembled-text-per-id, tracked-id count, and global memory bounds.

Reverse channel (activation/close/alive/query replies arriving terminal->child on stdin) is phase 2 via the parent-owned tipre-terminal-io shared I/O capability. The p=?/p=alive responder question is explicitly OPEN: the human OSC 7501 reply selection does NOT extend to OSC 99 virtual-delivery/alive semantics, and record-only observation must never be presented as evidence of actual OS delivery.
design: PROPOSED design pointer, not acceptance: /design/notifications/notifications0.glm53m.md (OSC 99 authoritative brief, cap accounting, responder boundaries). Provenance: opencode://ses_ec7f4e3bcffeQTeR4NqyDYJxS7.
acceptance_criteria: Parser unit tests: framing with empty metadata; all four payload placements; chunked assembly across multiple sequences; base64 decode; close-by-id; malformed-id rejection; per-sequence, per-id assembled, count, and global bounds enforced without unbounded memory (including a maximal encoded chunk that the old cap would have dropped). Outstanding-view lifecycle tests incl. documented loss of intermediate events under coalescing. A written responder decision naming the virtual-delivery implications precedes any reply behavior.

title: Parse and log OSC 777 notify events (title/body)
description:
Current surface: OSC 777 bytes relay unrecorded (src/osc.rs finish_osc leaves param 777 unmatched); the outer terminal already receives them.

Scope: route OSC param 777 in src/osc.rs to a Notify capture accepting '777;notify;title;body' with BEL or ST termination and tolerant arity (missing body tolerated; only the urxvt 'notify' command is recorded — other 777 commands pass through unrecorded). Record a timestamped event (protocol, title, body) into the epic's bounded recent-event window. No re-emit, no strip; delivery unchanged.
design: PROPOSED design pointer, not acceptance: /design/notifications/notifications0.glm53m.md (OSC 777 brief + parser design). Provenance: opencode://ses_ec7f4e3bcffeQTeR4NqyDYJxS7.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests in osc.rs: BEL and ST terminators; title-only (missing body) and full forms captured; non-notify 777 commands produce no event. Relay integration test: byte stream unchanged and event recorded in the window.

title: Observe and retain child desktop-notification events (OSC 9/777/99)
description:
Current surface: OSC 9, 777, and 99 bytes relay to the outer terminal unrecorded (src/osc.rs finish_osc returns None for these params), so child-issued desktop notifications leave no observable trace in the proxy.

Scope: observe notification events across the three wire conventions — bare OSC 9 text (iTerm2/ConEmu family), OSC 777 notify (urxvt; title/body), kitty OSC 99 (metadata/payload framing, chunked assembly, id-keyed update/close) — into a transient, bounded recent-event window with timestamps, plus a derived, coalesced outstanding-id view for OSC 99. The window is lossy process-lifetime event observation, NOT an owned durable append-only history: Kopacetic owns historical retention per the shell-tracking division, and coalescing can lose intermediate events. Delivery stays unchanged (observe-and-pass-through; notifications never re-emit implicitly). Reconnect summaries, notification filtering, and any proxy-side virtual-delivery/alive answering are out of scope and unselected. Publication rides the parent-owned tracking/Kopacetic boundary. Reverse-channel observation uses the parent-owned tipre-terminal-io shared I/O capability.
design: PROPOSED design pointer, not acceptance: /design/notifications/notifications0.glm53m.md. Provenance: opencode://ses_ec7f4e3bcffeQTeR4NqyDYJxS7.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A child emitting each of the three conventions produces timestamped recorded events without any change to the relayed byte stream. 2) OSC 99 chunked multi-part notifications assemble per id before recording. 3) The outstanding-id view reflects create/update/close transitions and is documented as coalesced/lossy. 4) Bounded memory holds under pathological streams (maximal 4096-byte encoded chunks that exceed the current data cap, unbounded chunk chains, id floods) per the design's whole-body/per-id/count/global cap accounting. 5) Event window snapshots into SessionExit.

title: Keep shell tracking lightweight across many proxy instances
description:
Capability: run term-preserver as an ordinary per-shell wrapper at many-instance scale with low private memory, idle CPU, wakeups, file descriptors and startup cost. Existing core is synchronous with relay/signal/resize workers; adding status records, capability replies and persistence must preserve that lightweight role.

Establish a measured baseline for idle shells, active output, status bursts and short-lived storage publications. Compare tracking-disabled and tracking-enabled configurations, optional regex/tmux features and selected backend profiles. Attribute private/PSS memory rather than multiplying total RSS or binary size as if shared pages were private. Investigate idle polling, redundant state copies, per-byte allocations, worker lifetime and database handle lifetime. The user explicitly wants short-lived writers, not a database kept open by every shell.

Choose optimizations from evidence; preserve relay ordering, protocol limits, terminal/job-control behavior, status responder ordering and final-state publication. No mandatory async runtime, persistent database owner or broad performance framework is implied. Related owner-native storage work: kop-collections-turso-writers and kop-collections-caminus-writers in ~/src/kopacetic.
acceptance_criteria:
A reproducible workload records startup cost, private/PSS memory, idle CPU/wakeups, thread/FD counts and throughput across representative instance counts.
Before/after results attribute costs to PTY core, protocol tracking and selected backend, including idle and burst behavior.
Selected optimizations reduce measured many-instance cost without unbounded buffers or hidden drop of required protocol state.
Short-lived storage handles are released after publication and contention is bounded without busy spinning.
PTY and protocol/responder regressions remain covered; record the actual accepted footprint goals from measurements rather than claiming unmeasured lightness.
notes: User explicitly commissioned many-instance lightness work. Source: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Expose per-pane tmux progress with explicit observation scope
description: Extend existing local tmux introspection with pane_pb_state/pane_pb_progress when available. An outside proxy sees only tmux's conditional selected-pane re-emission; sampling exposes retained progress for other panes. Keep per-pane sampled state distinct from the direct child-stream progress slot, recording source and sample time. Do not infer remote shell identity from a local connection wrapper. Reuse the current poll sampler; future control-mode freshness remains tipre-tmux-control-mode and resampling remains tipre-tmux-resample. Evidence: design/tracking/tmux-osc94.glm53fx.md.
acceptance_criteria:
A local multi-pane fixture exposes separate active/background pane progress with pane identity.
Missing progress formats are treated as unsupported rather than hidden/zero or a whole-session failure.
Direct OSC, tmux projection, and sampled pane state remain distinguishable.
No assertion that OSC 7501 crosses tmux normally; documented inside/outside placement agrees with the actual source path.
notes: Commissioned capability surface and prospective work. Session: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Publish shell snapshots through Kopacetic without blocking terminal relay
description: Add a selected-backend publisher with Caminus first and a narrow adapter boundary for later Turso/9P integration. Publish initial registration, accepted updates and final post-drain lifecycle state under the shell's stable key. Store calls run on a worker outside the relay and observed-state mutex. Bound pending work and allow latest-state coalescing, recording sequence/timestamps and making its loss of intermediate history explicit. Preserve meaningful backend failures and keep shell I/O usable. No shared registry/index or historical log is invented in term-preserver. Owner-native prerequisites and current guarantees: ~/src/kopacetic/doc/consumer/term-preserver.md; kop-collections-writer and kop-collections-caminus-writers.
acceptance_criteria:
Two proxy processes persist independent entries in one configured Caminus collection and fresh readers can reopen successful final writes.
Slow/failing storage does not block relay or indefinitely delay shell exit; latest dirty state and failures remain inspectable.
Reset and lifecycle updates are published in order; final snapshot follows drained output.
Backend selection does not change entity identity or terminal-state semantics.
Document actual Caminus visibility/failure behavior and coalescing limits; no claim of lossless history or atomic publication beyond the backend contract.
notes:
Commissioned capability surface and prospective work. Session: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F
Human clarified that persistence writers must be short-lived: open -> put -> release all store/connection/database handles per publication or explicitly bounded batch; the shell/worker can remain alive. Shared Turso requires bounded contention/retry and verified handle release, not an assumed permanent database owner. Follow kop-collections-turso-writers and kop-collections-writer in ~/src/kopacetic. Also coordinate many-instance measurements with tipre-tracking-lightness. Source: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Represent each observed shell lifetime as a stable typed entity
description: Define the shell-state payload and identity boundary used by storage. Use Kopacetic EntityIdentity with a unique shell lifetime name, stable across updates; PID, host, process-start evidence, title and tmux pane are attributes. Nested proxies receive new IDs with optional parent links. Include lifecycle/exit, sequence/timestamps, existing title/icon/color slots, independent progress, and program-status records. An outer connection wrapper must be labeled as connection/stream scope rather than impersonating every remote shell. Use a Facet-compatible DTO: indexed color entries and status IDs as data avoid backend-hostile map keys. Generic key equality belongs to kop-collections-identity.
acceptance_criteria:
Two simultaneous shells and nested shells have distinct keys; updates to one lifetime retain its key.
Unobserved and explicit clear/hidden states remain distinct.
The DTO retains title/icon/colors, 9;4, 7501 and process lifecycle without conflating their IDs.
Representative values including slash/dot status IDs and palette indices round-trip through the initial adapter.
Exited entities retain final evidence; process death does not trigger automatic collection deletion.
notes: Commissioned capability surface and prospective work. Session: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Provide a shell-compatible entry point with an explicit inner zsh
description: Provide the proposed term-preserver-shell executable/entry surface suitable for a terminal's shell setting or passwd shell path. Resolve an explicit real zsh independently of SHELL, prevent self-execution through symlinks/aliases, preserve login argv[0] and shell arguments including -c and its following positional arguments. Keep SHELL naming the public tracking wrapper so subsequent shell launches are tracked, while nested wrappers allocate fresh identities. Non-TTY invocations exec the real shell with inherited streams. Distinguish default command absence from Config.command's current [$SHELL] fallback, which active launch resolution can mistake for an explicit job. Related tipre-526 owns quoting repair for the separate composable launcher.
acceptance_criteria:
Login, interactive, -c with positional parameters, and non-TTY pipeline invocations preserve shell semantics and exact argv.
SHELL naming this wrapper does not recurse; direct/symlink inner self-selection is rejected clearly.
An installed executable path can be used without embedding flags in a passwd shell entry.
Interactive use selects one-shot cleanup; the real shell's status propagates.
The distinction between public shell, inner executable, and explicit trailing command is documented.
notes: Commissioned capability surface and prospective work. Session: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Run a tracked child once and propagate its exit status
description: Expose a one-shot lifecycle alongside the current unconditional RetryLoop. Reuse PTY creation, relay, signal forwarding and terminal restoration; on child completion drain output, finalize observed state and exit with the child's status. Shell mode produces no retry prompt, extra stdout status line or forced title/status restoration. Tracking selection is independent of reconnect policy, allowing connection wrappers to publish too. Keep reconnect behavior selectable through its existing entry path.
acceptance_criteria:
Normal and signal exits return the specified shell-compatible status with cooked terminal restored.
No retry keys or prompt are requested in one-shot mode.
Final output is drained before exit-state capture; TERM/HUP and EOF terminate coherently.
Existing retry mode still permits retry and quit.
PTY integration covers child output, resize, foreground interruption and cleanup.
notes: Commissioned capability surface and prospective work. Session: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Answer OSC 7501 capability queries from tracking mode
description: Human-selected capability: tracking mode advertises the status store even behind an unaware terminal or tmux. Consume OSC 7501;? and inject exactly one capability reply into child PTY input, listing supported states/kinds. Do not forward the intercepted query to the outer terminal; continue forwarding actual reports. Serialize injected replies with user-input writes and ensure a following primary DA query (CSI c) cannot race ahead of the status reply. When tracking is disabled, keep the ordinary outer-terminal query/reply path. Presentation is independent: recording status does not require synthesizing titles. Current relay has one stdin-owned PTY writer and no responder; establish a narrow input-write ownership seam.
acceptance_criteria:
An emitter detects support with an unaware outer terminal and emits a report that is retained.
Exactly one reply is delivered when the outer terminal also supports 7501; intercepted queries do not reach it.
Query plus CSI c in one read produces the status reply before the DA probe can produce an earlier reply.
Fragmented queries, concurrent user input and child exit preserve complete reply bytes and resource cleanup.
Disabled tracking passes queries unchanged; replies expose capabilities only, never stored records.
notes:
Commissioned capability surface and prospective work. Session: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F
Architectural review factored reusable terminal I/O into tipre-terminal-io-input and tipre-terminal-io-output; this ticket now depends on those capabilities and owns only OSC7501 response/interception semantics. Notification feedback and color querying consume shared I/O independently instead of depending on this entire protocol. Proposal: design/terminal-io/coordination0.gpt6a.md. Source: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Observe OSC 7501 hierarchical program-status records
description: Implement Program Status Protocol revision 0.4 report parsing and a bounded terminal-local record set. Each report replaces the addressed record completely; root and hierarchical child records coexist; clear removes a subtree. Preserve explicit app versus ancestor inheritance, typed state/kind/progress and decoded title/message. Record IDs are payload-local, not shell entity keys. Validate before mutation, including whole-sequence size and base64/control-character limits. Queries are recognized separately from reports. Evidence: design/tracking/osc-protocols.glm53m.md and https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status.
acceptance_criteria:
Replacement removes fields omitted by the new report; subtree clear respects segment boundaries.
Malformed IDs never fall back to root; unknown states do not mutate records; unknown keys follow the specification.
Whole-sequence 4096-byte, text, ID-depth and record-count limits are enforced; an invalid whole report leaves state unchanged.
Inherited app responds to ancestor changes without rewriting child reports.
Queries and ordinary unknown sequences do not mutate state, and reports retain outgoing bytes.
notes: Commissioned capability surface and prospective work. Session: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Apply prompt, reset and process lifetimes to program status
description: Couple the OSC 7501 reducer to the lifecycle edges specified by the protocol: OSC 133 A, attached-child exit and RIS. This is the narrow prompt/reset observation capability required for accurate status, not general command recording or screen emulation. Remove working/blocked on prompt/exit; retain done/error; explicitly choose the allowed idle policy. RIS removes every status record; alternate-screen changes and DECSTR do not. Drain final child output before applying exit so a final done/error report survives. Evidence: shell-tracking0.gpt6a.md, protocol revision 0.4.
acceptance_criteria:
Prompt and child exit drop working/blocked while retaining done/error; idle policy is documented and tested.
RIS clears all records; DECSTR and alternate-screen transitions preserve them.
Final report then exit ordering is covered by PTY integration.
These lifecycle changes reach snapshots/publication without replaying stale work into the outer terminal.
notes: Commissioned capability surface and prospective work. Session: opencode://ses_ec84404aaffeHUijDXZqczAc1F

title: Observe and retain OSC 9;4 progress state
description: Add a typed progress capture and independent observed slot alongside titles/colors. Current parameter 9 is forwarded but unrecorded. Capture state 0-4, optional percentage, report ordering and timestamps; distinguish never observed from explicitly hidden. Specify the accepted missing/trailing-value and out-of-range policy using ConEmu, Windows Terminal and tmux evidence rather than assuming they all agree. Preserve raw state/provided-value information needed to explain normalization. Do not impose Ghostty's presentation timeout or infer success from process exit. Title filters must not strip progress. Evidence: design/tracking/osc-protocols.glm53m.md and tmux-osc94.glm53fx.md.
acceptance_criteria:
BEL/ST and fragmented reports produce equivalent captures.
State-only, hidden, indeterminate, malformed and range-boundary cases follow the documented policy.
Unknown OSC 9 subcommands do not update progress and retain relay bytes.
Snapshots retain progress independently of title/color filters and child exit status.
Progress is not blindly replayed by --reemit-title.

title: Track and register shell-local terminal state
description:
Outcome: a shell-local PTY proxy that can be selected as the user's shell, runs an explicitly configured zsh, and publishes one Kopacetic entity per observed shell lifetime. Tracking also composes with the existing reconnecting launcher.

Existing surface: synchronous PTY relay; OSC 0/1/2 title/icon, 4/5 palette/special colors, 10/11/12 colors, and 104/105/110/111/112 resets; independent title strip/ignore filters; exit snapshots and optional re-emission; local tmux polling. Existing work anchors include tipre-keep-icon-osc, tipre-keep-color-osc, tipre-launcher, and tipre-tmux-session-id.

New surface: OSC 9;4 progress; OSC 7501 hierarchical status plus prompt/reset/exit lifetimes; proxy-owned capability responses; shell-compatible invocation and one-shot lifecycle; typed shell identity/snapshots; bounded asynchronous-to-the-relay Kopacetic publication. Caminus is the first desired backend. Kopacetic owns generic collections, backend concurrency, discovery and history (kop-collections in ~/src/kopacetic).

Per-shell truth is observed before tmux consumes it. Outside-tmux selected-pane projection is a distinct source. Existing title-preserver attachment policy (tipre-session-engine) remains related work, not a prerequisite for every observer. Human selected research/design and ticket commissioning; these tickets describe prospective implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
Each child capability has an explicit public behavior, state/lifetime contract, and verification.
A configured shell-entry invocation runs zsh without recursion, tracks status and title, persists a distinct shell entity, and exits with its child without a reconnect prompt.
Tracking-mode OSC 7501 detection works even when the outer terminal does not support it, with one ordered reply owner.
Two shells publish distinct entities through the selected backend without relay-blocking storage I/O.
Current, new, and future capabilities are documented with their owner-native ticket pointers; historical views remain Kopacetic-owned.
